Heavens (Biblical)
HEV-uhnz
noun
Hebrew shamayim (H8064, always plural in Hebrew), Greek ouranos (G3772) — the sky, the visible heavens, and the dwelling place of God; Paul refers to a "third heaven" (2 Cor 12:2) suggesting the biblical cosmology distinguishes three: (1) atmosphere, (2) stellar heavens, (3) dwelling place of God.

📖 Biblical Definition

Heavens in biblical cosmology is regularly three-layered. The Hebrew word shamayim is always plural (literally "heavens"), and Paul references a "third heaven" in 2 Corinthians 12:2 ("I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago...such an one caught up to the third heaven"), which he immediately equates with "paradise" (12:4). The traditional understanding of the three heavens: (1) the FIRST heaven is the atmosphere — where birds fly, clouds drift, and weather happens (Gen 1:20 — fowl that fly in the open firmament of heaven; Jer 4:25 — the birds of the heavens); (2) the SECOND heaven is the stellar heavens — where sun, moon, and stars are set (Gen 1:14-17; Ps 19:1 — "the heavens declare the glory of God"); (3) the THIRD heaven is the dwelling place of God Himself — paradise (2 Cor 12:2-4; 1 Kings 8:30 — "in heaven thy dwelling place"; Ps 11:4 — "the LORD's throne is in heaven"). Christ ascended through all three heavens ("made higher than the heavens," Heb 7:26; "passed through the heavens," Heb 4:14) into the immediate presence of the Father. Stephen at his martyrdom saw "the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God" (Acts 7:56) — the third heaven momentarily made visible. The heavens are not metaphor; they are real layered realms, and Christ has gone into the highest of them as our forerunner (Heb 6:20). In the eschatology of 2 Peter 3:10-13 the first and second heavens "shall pass away with a great noise" — the atmosphere and stellar heavens dissolved in the final judgment — but the third heaven (God's dwelling) is eternal, and the new heavens promised (2 Pet 3:13; Rev 21:1) are renewals of the lower two for the saints to inhabit forever with God whose throne occupies the highest.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The three-layered biblical cosmology: (1) atmosphere, (2) stellar heavens, (3) dwelling place of God / paradise.

expand to see more

HEAVENS, noun, plural. The sky and the spiritual realms above; in biblical cosmology three layers: the first heaven (atmosphere), the second heaven (stellar realm), and the third heaven (dwelling place of God).

Hebrew shamayim (always plural) and Greek ouranos (used both singular and plural). Paul speaks of a "third heaven" in 2 Cor 12:2-4, equating it with paradise. Christ ascended through all three (Heb 4:14; 7:26). The first and second pass away in 2 Peter 3:10-13; the new heavens come (Rev 21:1).

📖 Key Scripture

2 Corinthians 12:2-4 — "I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven. And I knew such a man... how that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter."

Hebrews 4:14 — "Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession."

Psalm 19:1 — "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork."

2 Peter 3:13 — "Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Heavens is corrupted when the three-layered cosmology is collapsed into a single vague "sky/heaven" (losing the careful biblical distinction between created cosmos and dwelling place of God) or when the new-heavens-and-earth promise is reduced to disembodied soul-existence rather than the embodied physical renewal Scripture promises.

expand to see more

Three-layer collapse. Modern translations and casual reading often treat "heaven" as a single undifferentiated category. But biblical Hebrew shamayim is always plural, and Paul explicitly identifies a third heaven. The atmosphere (where birds fly), the stellar realm (where stars shine), and God's dwelling place (where Christ now intercedes) are three distinct biblical referents. To collapse them is to confuse, for example, the heavens that "shall pass away with a great noise" (2 Pet 3:10 — the atmosphere and stellar realms) with the heaven where God's throne is (which is eternal).

Disembodied-eternity reduction. The popular Christian imagination often pictures the afterlife as floating souls in a cloudy abstract heaven. But the biblical promise is NEW HEAVENS AND A NEW EARTH (2 Pet 3:13; Rev 21:1) — embodied, physical, renewed creation. The atmosphere and stellar realms pass away to be remade; the third heaven (God's dwelling) descends and becomes the city we inhabit (Rev 21:2-3). Our eternal hope is not the third heaven AS WE NOW KNOW IT but the third heaven JOINED TO renewed earth — God dwelling with men permanently in a physical New Jerusalem.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew shamayim (H8064, always plural), Greek ouranos (G3772) — the three-layered heavens of biblical cosmology.

expand to see more

Hebrew shamayim (H8064) — heavens; ALWAYS plural in Hebrew (the form is dual or plural)

Greek ouranos (G3772) — heaven; used both singular and plural; Paul references the "third heaven" at 2 Cor 12:2

Three layers: (1) atmosphere (Gen 1:20), (2) stellar heavens (Gen 1:14-17; Ps 19:1), (3) dwelling place of God (1 Kings 8:30; Ps 11:4; 2 Cor 12:2-4)

Christ ascended THROUGH the heavens (Heb 4:14; 7:26) — from earth, through atmosphere and stellar realm, into the immediate presence of the Father

Usage

"Paul knew a man caught up to the third heaven — where God's throne is and paradise opens."

"The heavens are three-layered: atmosphere, stars, and the dwelling place of God; Christ has gone through all three for us."

"The new heavens and earth Peter promised are not disembodied existence but embodied renewal — God dwelling with men in a physical city forever."
